group_by.name: group_by
group_by.label: Grouping
group_by.format: comma-separated column names, coarse to fine, or all

recommend.name: a region and the countries inside it, a city too fine and a column with one value
a country that does not sit inside one region stays out
a column whose groups average under 30 records is not usable
no usable column recommends nothing, so the Grouping stays all

effective.name: small countries move up to their region, and a region still too small moves up to Global
all puts every record in one Global group
one column: a group too small goes straight to Global
three levels: small cities join their country, small countries join their region
the same city name in two countries stays two groups
a time series counts periods, not records: many records over few periods still move up

default.name: 1,000 records run on all of them
999 records run on all of them
718,931 records with only a date key run first on about 1,000 records, never a recent period by default
718,931 records with nothing to group by run first on the first 1,000 records, never everything
a count the metadata does not hold runs first on records, never everything
1,001 records of a standalone technique run first on records
a time series with a group column runs first on about 1,000 records in whole groups
a technique with a group column runs first on about 1,000 records in whole groups
a date column alone still runs first on about 1,000 records, never a recent period by default
5,000 records with nothing to group by run first on the first 1,000 records, never everything
a star-schema forecast with a store key and a date key runs first on about 1,000 records in whole groups
a time series with no group column runs first on the first 1,000 records, never a recent period by default
a standalone technique with no date column runs first on records

refused.name: a recent period without a date column
refused.reason: First run on a recent period needs the date column of main.sales.orders

refused.name: groups without a group column
refused.reason: First run on groups needs a column of main.sales.orders that groups its records

refused.name: a scope that does not exist
refused.reason: First run is 'everything', which is not one of all, groups, recent, records

scope_column.name: the finest column of a Grouping of columns
a Grouping of all falls back to the use case group column
no Grouping falls back to the use case group column
a custom Grouping is refused, since Inspire runs no typed SQL
scope_column.refused: the Grouping is 'custom': Inspire does not run SQL typed into Grouping or First run

logged.name: a scoped run against the earlier run on its scope
a use case without the First run, as before
a run without a scope skips an earlier run that recorded one
a run on everything against the earlier run on everything
the first run on a scope marks nothing

named_time.name: the event date role names the time column first
the judged date key reached through a date table comes before the judged time column
the judged time column of the table
a column of another table is never the time column (must-exclude)

time_source.name: a DATE column of the table is the time column
a date key joined to a dated table is the time column, read through that table's date
the named date key wins over the first one
a dated column of the table wins over a joined date key
a named column that is neither dated nor joined gives way to the table's date
a date key whose joined table holds no date is no time column (must-exclude)
an integer date key with no join is no time column (must-exclude)
a join to a table that is not catalog.schema.table is ignored (must-exclude)
columns that cannot be read keep the named column
columns that cannot be read and no named column give no time column

time_refs.name: only date-named and named columns ask for their joined table, once
a named key that is not date-named asks too
